definition: Expunge means to obliterate or erase completely.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word expunge. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know expunge should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The treaty's final clause expunged the old debts from every ledger on both sides of the border.
Blot is far milder than expunge — ink smeared over the entry, which a patient eye can still read beneath the stain, while an expunged record leaves nothing behind to read at all.
Erase is milder than expunge even when it is clean: an erased line can survive in copies and carbon sheets, while an expunged record is destroyed everywhere, as though never made.

Delete means to remove an entry from a file or document, but copies often survive on backups or in other drawers. Expunge goes all the way: the record is destroyed everywhere, officially and completely, as though it had never been made.

Redact means to black out sensitive parts of a document so readers cannot see them, while the document itself survives, bars and all. Expunge is total: nothing is hidden behind a bar, because the entry itself ceases to exist anywhere.

When the tribunal's ruling came down, the cycling federation did not merely add an asterisk to Danek Voss's seven summer victories.
It voted to expunge them: the results were struck from the official database, the printed annuals were reissued without his name, and the trophies were recalled and melted.
Even the finish-line photograph that had hung in the federation lobby came down, its frame reused for the new champion.
Race historians grumbled that the record now showed seven contests with no winner at all, as if those afternoons had never been raced.
